findings.title: Breaking API Change
findings.body: `offer_throughput` and `populate_query_metrics` were positional parameters in the sync `create_database` and `create_database_if_not_exists`. They are now keyword-only, and any extra positional argument raises `TypeError`. Existing calls like `client.create_database("db", None, 400)` will now fail at runtime. If this break is intended, it should be called out in the changelog. Otherwise, consider keeping positional support with a deprecation warning.

findings.title: Hook Signature Change
findings.body:
The previous async docstring declared `response_hook` as `Callable[[Dict[str, str], Dict[str, Any]], None]`. The new code calls it with a single argument, `response_hook(self.client_connection.last_response_headers)`. Existing user hooks with two required parameters will raise `TypeError`.

This affects `create_database` and both the read path and the create path of `create_database_if_not_exists`. It is uncertain whether the old runtime actually passed two arguments. If it did, this is a silent breaking change for async users.

findings.title: Fragile Test
findings.body: `test_default_max_concurrency_uses_python_default` hardcodes `min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4)`. Since Python 3.13, `ThreadPoolExecutor` uses `os.process_cpu_count()`, which respects CPU affinity. In containers or CI runners with restricted affinity, the assertion fails. The test also reads the private `_max_workers` attribute, and it only checks a CPython detail rather than SDK behavior. Consider asserting that `ThreadPoolExecutor` is constructed with `max_workers=None` (e.g., via `patch`) instead.
